1.explanation: The `WebGLTileLayer.render` override in WebGLTile.js never intersects the map frame extent with the layer’s own `extent` property, so sources are fetched and drawn beyond the user-defined bounds. In the renderer (TileLayer.js), `getRenderExtent` is supposed to clip the map's frame extent to the layer extent but is left unimplemented, and `prepareFrameInternal` enqueues tiles over the full frame rather than the clipped region. By implementing `getRenderExtent` to intersect `frameState.extent` with `this.layer.getExtent()` and updating `prepareFrameInternal` (and/or `render`) to use that clipped extent, the renderer will correctly limit drawn tiles to the original layer extent.
1.bug_scenario: A COG (cloud-optimized GeoTIFF) is displayed using a WebGLTile layer with an explicit `extent` option (red box). However the rendered raster is not clipped to that extent: it overruns the red bounding box, drawing black backgrounds and stray tile edges outside the intended area. As you zoom in, the drawn area also narrows in an uncontrolled way. In short, the layer’s configured extent is not being enforced in the WebGL renderer.

2.explanation:
• src/ol/layer/WebGLTile.js::WebGLTileLayer#getSources and #render always use the full frameState.extent (map viewport) to pick and draw tiles, ignoring the layer’s own extent property. This means no clipping against the COG’s true bounding box.  
• src/ol/renderer/webgl/TileLayer.js::WebGLTileLayerRenderer#getRenderExtent is currently a stub; without a proper intersection of the frame extent and the layer extent, tiles outside the layer boundary continue to be enqueued and drawn.  
• In prepareFrameInternal and enqueueTiles, the (unclipped) extent drives tile lookup and queuing logic, so tiles beyond the true extent are fetched and rendered.  
To fix the bug, getRenderExtent must be implemented to intersect the frame extent with the layer extent, and prepareFrameInternal/ enqueueTiles must use that clipped extent. Additionally, WebGLTileLayer.render (and its getSources call) should respect the layer’s extent when choosing which tile sources to draw.
2.bug_scenario: The user is displaying a single-band Cloud‐Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) with WebGLTileLayer and setting the layer’s native extent to the TIFF’s real bounding box. In QGIS and on a 2D map, the image stays strictly within that extent rectangle. However, when rendered with WebGLTileLayer on the web, portions of the tile appear far outside the defined red‐box extent (and the rendered image slants/narrows as you zoom in). In other words, tiles that should be clipped at the layer’s extent are still fetched or drawn outside of it.
